text: Quine's "Epistemology Naturalized" (1969) makes which radical methodological proposal?
choices: Epistemology should become a chapter of empirical psychology, studying how humans actually form beliefs
Epistemology should be pursued purely a priori, wholly independent of natural science
The normative question of justification is the only legitimate epistemological question
Philosophy of mind should defer entirely to Husserlian phenomenology
explanation: Quine urged replacing the foundationalist project of justification with an empirical account of belief-formation -- epistemology as 'a chapter of psychology.' Option B is the traditional rationalism he rejects, C is the normative project he wants to naturalize away, and D is unrelated; critics charge that his program drops the normative dimension entirely.
